display.purpose: Hero headlines and page-level H1s only. Rare by design so it stays a signal.

body.purpose: Every other word in the interface. Chosen specifically to replace Inter.

mono.purpose: Numbers, dates, streak counts, the AI Quick Add input - anything that is data, not prose.

shadows.name: hover-lift
shadows.purpose: Interactive cards (Dashboard stats, feature cards) on hover only - tinted to the primary hue, never a generic black shadow.

shadows.name: modal-glass-border
shadows.purpose: Inner highlight on glass modal edges to simulate physical refraction.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default easing for every non-spring transition in the system (expo-out).

motion.name: spring-snappy
motion.purpose: Buttons, checkboxes, toggles, drag-release, sliding tab indicators.

motion.name: stagger-list
motion.purpose: Sibling delay for any list/grid reveal.

motion.name: view-transition-root
motion.purpose: Whole-view cross-fade when switching between app-interior screens.

motion.name: view-transition-shared-element
motion.purpose: Task rows sharing a view-transition-name between Dashboard and Task Manager morph using this duration.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The default call-to-action button. Near-white fill in dark mode, spring press feedback.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--primary, #fafafa); color: var(--primary-foreground, #171717); border: none; border-radius: 8px; padding: 10px 16px; font-family: Geist, system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 500; font-size: 14px; cursor: pointer; transition: transform 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), opacity 0.2s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { transform: translateY(-2px); opacity: 0.92; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.97); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ring, #fafafa); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Destructive Button
components.description: Delete/remove actions. The only button variant carrying the system's one semantic color.
components.css: .ds-btn-destructive { background: hsl(4 68% 60%); color: hsl(0 0% 7%); border: none; border-radius: 8px; padding: 10px 16px; font-family: Geist, system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 500; font-size: 14px; cursor: pointer; transition: transform 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), opacity 0.2s; } .ds-btn-destructive:hover { opacity: 0.88; } .ds-btn-destructive:active { transform: scale(0.97); }

components.name: Card
components.description: Flat-at-rest content card with a hairline border; picks up a primary-tinted shadow and lift only on hover.
components.css: .ds-card { background: hsl(0 0% 7%); color: hsl(0 0% 98%); border: 1px solid hsl(0 0% 15%); border-radius: 8px; padding: 16px; transition: transform 0.3s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), box-shadow 0.3s; } .ds-card:hover { transform: translateY(-4px); box-shadow: 0 16px 36px -18px hsl(0 0% 98% / 0.35); } .ds-card-label { font-family: Geist, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; color: hsl(0 0% 65%); margin: 0 0 4px; } .ds-card-value { font-family: 'Geist Mono', monospace; font-size: 24px; font-weight: 700; margin: 0; }

components.name: Badge
components.description: Secondary metadata chip - tag counts, priority labels, AI indicators.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; background: hsl(0 0% 15%); color: hsl(0 0% 98%); border-radius: 9999px; padding: 2px 10px; font-family: Geist, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; }

components.name: Task Row (signature)
components.description: The app's most-interacted-with component: spring checkbox, completion burst, drag-to-complete/delete affordance icons flanking it.
components.html: Finish project proposalHigh
components.css: .ds-task-row { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; padding: 10px 14px; border-radius: 8px; transition: background 0.2s; } .ds-task-row:hover { background: hsl(0 0% 15%); } .ds-task-checkbox { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 20px; height: 20px; border-radius: 6px; background: hsl(0 0% 98%); transition: transform 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); } .ds-task-row:active .ds-task-checkbox { transform: scale(0.85); } .ds-task-title { flex: 1; font-family: Geist, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; color: hsl(0 0% 98%); } .ds-task-priority { font-family: Geist, sans-serif; font-size: 11px; padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 9999px; background: hsl(0 0% 15%); color: hsl(0 0% 98%); }

components.name: Sidebar Nav Item
components.description: Active state uses a shared-layout glow chip and accent bar that slides between items rather than a hard swap.
components.html: Dashboard
components.css: .ds-nav-item { position: relative; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; padding: 8px 12px; border-radius: 8px; font-family: Geist, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; color: hsl(0 0% 65%); text-decoration: none; transition: color 0.2s, background 0.2s; } .ds-nav-item:hover { color: hsl(0 0% 98%); background: hsl(0 0% 15%); } .ds-nav-item-active { color: hsl(0 0% 98%); background: hsl(0 0% 98% / 0.08); } .ds-nav-bar { position: absolute; left: -12px; top: 4px; bottom: 4px; width: 2px; border-radius: 9999px; background: hsl(0 0% 98%); }

components.name: Tab Trigger (Feature Grid)
components.description: Pill tab with a layoutId-shared sliding indicator. Label sits above the indicator with explicit z-index (a real stacking-context bug was found and fixed here: a naive negative z-index on the indicator rendered it behind the trigger's own background, making active-tab text unreadable).
components.css: .ds-tab-trigger { position: relative; border: 1px solid hsl(0 0% 15%); border-radius: 9999px; padding: 6px 16px; font-family: Geist, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; background: transparent; cursor: pointer; } .ds-tab-trigger-active { border-color: hsl(0 0% 98%); } .ds-tab-indicator { position: absolute; inset: 0; border-radius: 9999px; background: hsl(0 0% 98%); } .ds-tab-label { position: relative; z-index: 10; color: hsl(0 0% 9%); }

narrative.overview: Monotask is a task, habit, and calendar app for people managing focus across too many apps. The design system takes the product's own thesis and applies it to itself: just as the product removes app-switching, the interface removes the accent color, the decorative motion, and the competing visual signals that most SaaS products lean on. What's left is a strict monochrome palette, two typefaces doing very deliberate jobs, and a motion language that exists to demonstrate the product working, not to decorate around it. The system runs two registers: Operate mode (the authenticated app) is tight and shadcn-scaled because the visitor is completing a task; Persuade mode (landing/auth) is looser and more cinematic because the visitor is deciding whether to trust the product. Dark is the default theme system-wide.
keyCharacteristics: Pure monochrome neutrals, zero decorative accent color
One real semantic exception: a muted brick-red destructive hue
Dark-by-default, light mode fully inverted and supported
Space Grotesk for display, Geist for body/UI, Geist Mono for numbers/data
Motion is physics-based (spring) or a single shared expo-out ease, never a default CSS ease
Flat-by-default surfaces; real elevation reserved for floating layers
Two radius registers by surface type: tight in the app, soft/pill-heavy on marketing surfaces

rules.name: The Color Consistency Lock Rule
rules.body: Once the palette is monochrome-plus-destructive-red, it stays that way everywhere. Tag creation is now grayscale-only too (a fixed 5-swatch picker); legacy/seeded tags predating this pass still carry saturated colors, a known inconsistency, not a two-tier design.

rules.name: The No Pure Black/White Rule
rules.body: Background and foreground extremes stop at hsl(0 0% 7%) / hsl(0 0% 98%). Pure #000/#fff are never used.

rules.name: The Eyebrow Restraint Rule
rules.body: Small uppercase-tracked labels above a heading appear on at most one section in every three.

rules.name: The Zero Em-Dash Rule
rules.body: No em-dash appears anywhere in shipped copy.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Shadow or glass appears only as a response to state.

rules.name: The One Radius Per Surface Rule
rules.body: A single view never mixes the Operate and Persuade radius scales.

dos: Do keep the palette strictly monochrome plus the one destructive red.
Do use Space Grotesk only at real display scale; Geist for everything else.
Do check every new animated component against prefers-reduced-motion as part of building it.
Do keep the app interior's radius scale and the marketing site's separate.
Do use tinted-shadow and glass techniques only for genuinely elevated/floating elements.
Do give every destructive action a real confirmation step.
Do use real, working component previews for any marketing demo, never a fake screenshot.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent color anywhere.
Don't default to Inter for new text.
Don't apply glassmorphism to primary content surfaces.
Don't add motion that isn't motivated by hierarchy, storytelling, feedback, or a state transition.
Don't use a flat CSS ease for anything that should feel physical.
Don't use an em-dash anywhere in shipped copy.
Don't repeat a page's title twice in one view.
Don't reopen tag colors to arbitrary hues without resolving the legacy-color inconsistency first.
Don't fire a toast for an action that already has its own visible state change.
Don't ship a second scroll-hijacked section on the landing page; one GSAP sticky-stack per page is the cap.
